transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Dora, a clinical conversational agent. I can help answer questions about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hello, yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should avoid any exercise for 1 week after surgery, but after that, you can go back to light exercise like gardening. However, you should avoid strenuous exercise for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to know, thanks! I've been very sensitive to bright light lately. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity is not normal, especially if your eye is also red and painful, and we may need to assess this further. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.text: No, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for all your help!
